title: Father the railroader; Norvo the youngest of four
summary: His father was night chief dispatcher for the Burlington; he names his brothers Howard and Glenn and sister Portia and says he was the youngest.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, it's a nice little town,my father was a railroader, he worked for the Burlington. Night chief dispatcher and then the night chief --
Uh-huh.
And --
Does that --
What?
Does he always have to be away at nights then?
Yes, he was at nights. He worked -- let's see, from 12:00 to 8:00 for awhile. Different hours --
Yeah, yeah.
-- you know they had three shifts and those things.
Yeah, yeah, yeah.
But there was a lot of coal going through. See the coal mines down in Herrin [Illinois] and lot of tra --
Yeah, yeah.
-- railroad traffic in those days.
Oh.
I had two brothers, and a sister, the oldest was Hoard, next was Glenn, and my sister was named Portia. I was the youngest.
Oh, you named your daughter after your sister, then.
Well my wife named her after --
Oh, how nice -- because I thought it was, you know --
Yeah, she liked the name so she wanted to name her --
So you were the youngest?
I was the young --
Of the four?
Of the four, yes I was the youngest.
Oh, how -- what.
They were two and a half years apart and I think I was six or eight years -- between my sister and I.
Yeah, I see. Oh, yeah. So your older (unintelligible) brother was quite a bit older.
